title: Reconcile refusal paths leave no outcome audit row
body:
## Summary
Pipeline::reconcile writes receipt.reporting_checked before reading and receipt.reporting_unmatched on a clean miss, but its four refusal paths return Invalid with no outcome row.

## Description
crates/table-app/src/reconciliation.rs:22 writes the pre-read row; :54 (page / total / size / no-200 guard), :60 (status not S), :66 (buyer row without a debit sign) and :81 (ambiguous: more than one match) return Error::Invalid with only the paypal_calls rows behind them. The success path writes confirm_reporting and the miss writes receipt.reporting_unmatched (:90), so the outcome most needing evidence (an ambiguous or contradicting statement) is the only one with no audit row (audit-logging technique write-chokepoint: every outcome through one recorded door). Fixed: a receipt.reporting_refused row with a fixed reason code before each Invalid. The action must be registered in table-ledger audit_detail.rs (field allowlist :141-142), table-runtime history/classify.rs (:240-242) and the client words (windows/main/logic.ts:703), all outside this context.

## Flow
- owner asks for the statement check on a RECEIPTED deal
- PayPal reporting answers two rows for the capture id (case 6 of own_account_reporting_requires_success_...)
- reconcile returns Invalid; audit_log holds reporting_checked and nothing after it
- fix: append receipt.reporting_refused {from,to,capture_id,reason} before each Invalid; register the action in the three readers

## Expected impact
Rewind and the audit reader show why a statement check refused, instead of a check that started and never ended. Could break: audit row counts pinned by the reporting test.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every reconcile outcome leaves an audit row
Before: 4 refusal paths, 0 outcome rows (cases 2, 5, 6, 8 of the reporting test)
After: 4 of 4 write receipt.reporting_refused
Method: simulation - read the paths against the test cases; the fix needs table-ledger audit_detail.rs, a sibling crate this wave
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
crates/table-app/src/reconciliation.rs:54, :60, :66, :81 return Err(Error::Invalid) with no append_audit
crates/table-ledger/src/audit_detail.rs:141-142 action allowlist
crates/table-runtime/src/history/classify.rs:240-242
instrument: extend own_account_reporting_requires_success_exact_capture_amount_currency_direction_and_complete_pages: cases 2|5|6|8 each carry exactly one receipt.reporting_refused row (0 today); cases 0|4 keep one reporting_unmatched

title: Pipeline::tick is a test-only loop that diverges from the production scheduler
body:
## Summary
Pipeline::tick has no production caller; about 20 table-app test sites drive deadlines through it, while the runtime and the house run their own loops over live deals only.

## Description
crates/table-app/src/pipeline.rs:628 iterates ledger.list_deals() (every deal, terminal ones included) and calls rescue_tick / deadline_default per deal. Production never calls it: crates/table-runtime/src/scheduler.rs:16 iterates list_live_deals() and calls deadline_default at :95; services/house-seller/src/hosted.rs:908 does the same; crates/table-runtime/src/rescue.rs:292 calls rescue_tick. A grep for `.tick(` outside the table-app tests finds 0 calls of Pipeline::tick. The pinned loop is not the shipped loop, and its per-tick cost grows with history (2 ledger reads per terminal deal per tick). Fixed: tick iterates list_live_deals as the scheduler does, or the tests move to a helper that mirrors scheduler.rs.

## Flow
- grep `.tick(` across crates/ and services/: only crates/table-app/tests/{pipeline,gauntlet}.rs call Pipeline::tick
- scheduler.rs:16 and hosted.rs:908 iterate list_live_deals
- fix: tick takes list_live_deals (or is dropped and the tests ported)

## Expected impact
Deadline tests exercise the iteration production runs. Could break: a test relying on tick pruning the read state of a deal that went terminal outside the tick.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the tested deadline loop is the shipped loop
Before: 1 test-only loop over all deals vs 2 production loops over live deals; 0 production callers of Pipeline::tick
After: 0 divergent loops
Method: simulation - grep of callers; the visit count is not observable without a counter this round did not build
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
crates/table-app/src/pipeline.rs:628 for deal in self.wallet.ledger.list_deals()?
crates/table-runtime/src/scheduler.rs:16 list_live_deals
services/house-seller/src/hosted.rs:908 deadline_default
grep `.tick(`: crates/table-app/tests/pipeline.rs, crates/table-app/tests/gauntlet.rs only
instrument: a table-app test with 50 terminal deals and 1 live AUTHORIZED deal past its deadline: a counting PayPalApi/ledger wrapper shows tick visits only the live deal; the table-app and table-runtime suites stay green

title: Checklist host line hard-codes the sandbox allowlist the proto check owns
body:
## Summary
The approval checklist states the PayPal host allowlist as a literal at 3 sites in checks.rs, while the rule itself is a literal in table-proto settlement.rs.

## Description
crates/table-app/src/checks.rs:355, :367 and :376 write www.sandbox.paypal.com (and port 443) into the Layer-2 detail; crates/table-proto/src/settlement.rs:29-32 is the check that decides. A change to the allowlist (live mode, a second host) leaves the checklist telling the owner a rule the code no longer applies. Fixed: table-proto exports the host as a const and checks.rs formats it.

## Flow
- change the allowed host in settlement.rs approval_url
- the checklist detail still names www.sandbox.paypal.com

## Expected impact
Layer-2 detail stays true to the check behind it. Could break: nothing user-visible today.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source for the stated allowlist
Before: 4 literals of one rule (3 in checks.rs, 1 in settlement.rs)
After: 1 const, 3 uses
Method: simulation - grep; the const belongs in table-proto, outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: checks_tests: the host line detail contains the new table_proto sandbox-host const; seeding the const to another host fails the proto test and the checklist test together

title: read_state_of scans every schedule key for each deal on each tick
body:
## Summary
prune_read_state calls read_state_of, which walks every key of parked_read and rescue_read_backoff to find one deal's entries; the scheduler runs it per live deal per tick.

## Description
crates/table-app/src/pipeline/read_state.rs:169-181 filters all keys with key_names_deal; :107-114 calls it from prune_read_state, which runs after every deadline_default and rescue_tick. The maps are BTreeMap<String,_> keyed {deal}-{attempt}-{op} or deadline-read:{deal}, so one deal's entries are two contiguous ranges. At the cap (READ_STATE_CAP 4096 per map, read_state.rs:18) that is 8192 prefix checks per deal per tick. Fixed: range(id..) with a prefix take_while, plus one get of the deadline-read key.

## Flow
- N live deals, maps near the cap after a PayPal outage
- each 1 s tick: N x 8192 key checks
- fix: two range lookups, O(log M + k)

## Expected impact
Ticks stay flat while many reads are failing. Could break: an entry whose key shape differs from the two documented ones would be missed (none exist).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - per-deal schedule lookup cost
Before: O(M), up to 8192 key checks per deal per tick at the cap
After: O(log M + k)
Method: simulation - read the code; no timing probe was run (realistic maps are near-empty, so the gain shows only after an outage)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a #[cfg(test)] probe filling both maps to READ_STATE_CAP and timing 1000 read_state_of calls before/after, plus an equality test that the range lookup and the scan count the same entries for 100 random keys

title: A partly paid rescue invoice expires uncounted and unflagged
body:
## Summary
A rescue invoice PayPal reports PARTIALLY_PAID is read as still waiting, then expires at its deadline like an unpaid one: money arrived, nothing counts it and nothing asks the owner.

## Description
crates/table-app/src/rescue.rs rescue_poll matches PAID (nothing due) and CANCELLED (:595); PARTIALLY_PAID falls to `_ => Ok(false)` (:599). At the deadline crates/table-app/src/rescue/deadline.rs:53-99 reads once more, gets Ok(false), then apply_deadline_default (:97) ends the deal EXPIRED. SENT_STATUSES (rescue.rs:93) already treats PARTIALLY_PAID as proof the send went out, so the code knows the state. What the product does with part of a discounted cycle (count it, flag it for the owner, keep reading) is a product decision the design (DECISIONS 13) does not state.

## Flow
- owner approves a fix; the subscriber pays part of the invoice
- rescue_poll reads PARTIALLY_PAID -> Ok(false), every cadence
- deadline: one more read, Ok(false), deal EXPIRED, rescue_recovered unchanged, no attention item

## Expected impact
The owner learns that a subscriber paid something instead of seeing an expired fix. Could break: recovered totals, if partial amounts are counted.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a partial payment is surfaced, not silently expired
Before: PARTIALLY_PAID -> EXPIRED with 0 rows saying money arrived (walked through rescue_poll and rescue_deadline)
After: depends on the chosen behaviour (count, attention, or keep reading)
Method: simulation - three walked cases; the target behaviour is a product choice
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
crates/table-app/src/rescue.rs:599 _ => Ok(false) after PAID / CANCELLED arms
crates/table-app/src/rescue.rs:93 SENT_STATUSES includes PARTIALLY_PAID
crates/table-app/src/rescue/deadline.rs:97 apply_deadline_default after an Ok(false) read
instrument: tests/rescue.rs: the Invoicing double answers PARTIALLY_PAID with due_amount > 0; assert the chosen outcome at the deadline (today: EXPIRED, rescue_recovered empty, no attention item)
